data.description:
Operator-mode enablement, part 1 of 2. Full design: docs/ENABLEMENT.md (read it first — it is the spec).

WHAT: New subcommands 'enable' and 'disable'. 'enable' sets git config etch.enabled=true (common dir — shared by all worktrees/branches, never pushed) and writes the .etch ignore entries (.etch/* with !.etch/settings.json carve-out, plus .claude/settings.local.json) into .git/info/exclude. 'disable' sets etch.enabled=false. Every hook entrypoint gets a fast-exit guard: not a git repo, or etch.enabled=false → exit 0 before any other work.

COMPATIBILITY RULE: a repo with committed hooks and NO config key keeps capturing (team mode must not require 'etch enable'). Key absent = enabled when dispatched; etch.enabled=false is an explicit off-switch that wins over everything.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) enable → key set + excludes written, idempotent on rerun; (2) disable → all capture stops in main checkout AND worktrees, both dispatch modes; (3) team-mode repo with no key captures unchanged; (4) disabled-path latency within SPEC AC #13 budget — measure it; (5) tests via testutil temp repos incl. worktree cases.
data.title: etch enable/disable — git-config enablement switch + fast-exit guard

data.body: VALIDATION EVIDENCE: full go test suite green with -count=1 (16 packages) on the PR branch and on CI (GitHub Actions runs 27433694695, 27434292570, both pass). Binary-level acceptance tests cover real 'git worktree add' worktrees for enable/disable, team-mode no-key compat, and the non-git fast exit. Disabled-path latency measured over 50 real binary invocations: median 4.7ms / p90 5.0ms / max 5.1ms vs the 50ms SPEC AC #13 budget (independently re-measured by the code reviewer at median 5.57ms / max 6.14ms). Live end-to-end validation on the c11 pilot repo (enable + new-worktree capture) is scheduled after ETCH-48 merges, per the rollout plan.

Shipped operator-mode enablement part 1 (PR #2, squash-merged to main as e1ea295). New internal/enable package: 'enable' sets etch.enabled=true in the shared common config + writes a marker-delimited ignore block to .git/info/exclude (idempotent, byte-preserving, stale blocks refreshed in place); 'disable' sets etch.enabled=false — the explicit off-switch silencing all dispatch everywhere. All six hook entrypoints gated by a fast-exit guard ahead of stdin: spawn-free common path (manual .git/gitdir/commondir resolution + bounded config scan, git-config fallback for GIT_DIR/include directives), stdin drained before exit so dispatchers never see EPIPE. Key absent = enabled (team-mode compat); malformed values fail open. Measured disabled path: median 4.7ms / p90 5.0ms / max 5.1ms vs 50ms budget. Deliberate behavior change: hooks outside a git repo now exit 0 silently (supersedes ETCH-35's fail-visible contract for that path only; in-repo failures stay loud). Lattice plan-review and code-review both PASS; all four code-review minors folded in (.git symlink via Stat, section-header comments, ENABLEMENT.md scope note, latency-assertion deviation acknowledged in PR). 26 new tests incl. real worktree cases. Remaining: worktree stamping + post-checkout propagation + dedupe land in ETCH-48.
